title.narrative: Output 1.4. Increased capacity of Member States to improve social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative: 1. An analysis of the effectiveness of existing Tripartite consultative committees at the federal and provincial levels is produced and used by the Governments to discuss and revisit the use of these fora to meet the objectives set out in the TORs for these structures and to uphold the requirements of C144. 2. Government established and notified an FOA/CB's government committee. The committee is overseeing the process of engagement with provincial stakeholders and social partners gradually but steadily carrying out discourses on changes in the existing law that will result in significant reforms on freedom of association and collective bargaining. 3. Social dialogue has been strengthened in 47 factories through formation of worker-management committees which is being used to bring meaningful changes at the unit level and to address enterprise-based issues. 4. Improving capacities of EOs and WOs to support compliance and influence compliance through dialogue at sectoral levels to support both EO and WO to better represent their members. This includes support to the implementation of the Memorandum of Understanding agreed by the Government of Pakistan and provincial governments of Sindh and Punjab. 5. Workers and Employers Bilateral Council of Pakistan(WEBCOP) and MNE Declaration focal point strengthened through the development of an action plan including the area of grievance handling/dispute resolution and industrial relations. • With support of the EU, the ILO facilitated capacity development of members of all Provincial Tripartite Consultative Committees (PTCC) and Federal Tripartite Consultative Committee (FTCC) on international labour standards (ILS), reporting obligations, ILO supervisory bodies, the 2023 ILS reporting obligation. • The briefing note on FTCC and PTCC has informed the Government about the working of these dialogue forums, capturing the current situation, and practices as well as identifying areas for future improvement of the mechanism. The briefing note aims to provide a summary of the current situation and practices within the Federal Tripartite Consultative Committee (FTCC) and Provincial Tripartite Consultative Committees (PTCCs) in Pakistan. It also identifies areas for future improvement. The objective is to enhance the utilization of FTCC and PTCC for strengthening the implementation and reporting on the ILS, discussing ILS ratifications, and improving coordination between the federal centre and provinces on these issues. The Government is using the briefing note to engage tripartite committee members at federal and provincial level to discuss challenges that can be collectively addressed to make these committees more effective • ILO developed a technical note on freedom of associations and collective bargaining (FOA/CB) and facilitated consultations for government, workers, and employers’ representatives. • ILO facilitated consultation on labour statistics concerning GSP+ compliance data collection. ILO developed a concept note on a pilot test of modules related to collective bargaining, freedom of association, forced labour and child labour in two provinces.

Output 7.2. Increased capacity of Member States to ensure safe and healthy working conditions

description.narrative: 1.In 2023, the Department of Labour in Sindh Province established a comprehensive Provincial OSH Programme, the result of collaboration with employers and workers and an inclusive process involving various stakeholders. During the process, 8 outcome areas were incorporated into the program encompassing a range of objectives, including raising public awareness about the importance of preventive safety and health practices, the enforcement of the Sindh Safety and Health Act of 2017, as well as Mining Laws. The program also aims to create industry-specific OSH standards, promote active engagement in workplace OSH committees and management systems, strengthen labour inspection, extend OSH protection to small enterprises and informal workplaces, ensure the mandatory reporting of occupational accidents and diseases, and enhance research, education, and training for OSH staff. 2.In Sindh Province, 29 enterprises operating in the textile sector, along with 5 business associations, underwent a capacity-building initiative to establish bipartite Workplace OSH Committees. Participants received comprehensive training on the functions and responsibilities of OSH workplace committees, the skill to identify OSH-related risks, and the ability to engage in constructive discussions to pinpoint areas requiring improvement. This initiative played a pivotal role in enhancing workplace safety within the textile sector and fostering a collaborative approach between employers and workers. 3.In 2023, a comprehensive national OSH profile was developed and launched. The profile serves as an invaluable repository of critical information and data related to OSH practices across Pakistan, including workplace regulations, incident reports, safety standards, and best practices. The profile informed the Gap Analysis of Conventions. 1.With funding from the EU, the ILO took proactive measures to facilitate the process of raising awareness and building the capacity of businesses in establishing OSH workplace committees. The ILO organized comprehensive training sessions and workshops, tailored to the specific needs of selected businesses in Sindh Province. Additionally, the ILO provided valuable resources, guidelines, and expert guidance to ensure that businesses had the necessary tools and knowledge to set up effective OSH committees. 2. ILO’s technical expertise was extended with funding from the EU to support the Government of Sindh in designing the consultative workshops with social partners and other stakeholders to formulate the OSH programme. The ILO also extended support in interpreting the ILO Conventions and their application through the various programme outcomes. 3.With support of the EU, the ILO provided technical support and guidance on the systematic gathering, validation, and organization of collected data. Moreover, the ILO assisted in the drafting of the national OSH profile. This involved synthesizing the collected data into a coherent and comprehensive document. ILO played a critical role in ensuring that the profile was not only informative but also aligned with ILO Standards.

description.narrative: • In 2023, The government has localised the ILO’s Strategic Compliance Planning methodology (SCP) to help labour inspectorates at the provincial level to efficiently plan and execute labour inspection activities with measurable improvements in labour law compliance using limited resources. In this regard, Capacity Development Workshops on Strategic Compliance Planning resulted in the identification of key challenges and pilot areas that the provincial governments advised to address to ensure adequate strengthening of labour inspection in line with the stipulations of Convention No.81. Two provincial Strategic Compliance Task Teams and two provincial Task Teams have initiated the effective implementation of the developed Strategic Compliance Plan in 2023. • 30 labour inspectors (5 females) from provincial Labour and Human Resource Departments of two provinces were trained on OSH labour inspection using the ILO tool « Work Improvements in Small Enterprises (WISE) methodologies and supporting the establishment of OSH committees at workplaces • With support from the EU, the ILO conducted capacity need a mapping of labour inspections of 4 provinces to identify gaps and design capacity development workshops customised for each province. ILO also supported convening and facilitating capacity development workshops on strategic compliance planning for four provincial Labour Inspectorates. ILO supported the development of terms of reference for the Strategic Compliance Task Teams and also facilitated the first meeting of the task team of Balochistan. • ILO supported facilitating capacity development of OSH inspectors from provinces Sindh and Balochistan on the ILO WISE tool and Workplace OSH Committee.
